newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: NAFTA critic Gephardt praises Mercosur trade bloc.
newsitem.headline: NAFTA critic Gephardt praises Mercosur trade bloc.

text.p: U.S. House of Representatives Democratic Leader Richard Gephardt, an outspoken critic of the North American Free Trade Agreement, praised the South American trade bloc Mercosur on Friday.
"I think Mercosur is a very positive development," Gephardt told reporters after meeting Argentine officials.

Gephardt, on a fact-finding tour of Chile, Argentina, Venezuela and Brazil, is one of the leading critics of NAFTA, which groups the United States with Canada and Mexico and which Chile has been waiting to join since 1994.
Asked in Chile if he would support U.S. President Bill Clinton's request for "fast-track" authority to negotiate new trade deals, such as Chile's, he answered only: "Let's see."
Gephardt told reporters in Argentina that his reservations about NAFTA were "about having provisions on social issues, labor rights, human rights and environmental protection."
But turning to Mercosur, a fledgling customs union formed by Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay, with Chile as an associate partner, Gephardt said:

"My sense is Mercosur is considering labor and environment issues along with the trade and economic issues. My hope is that eventually we can have a hemispheric, a North and South America free trade agreement."

The Democratic leader said he was "deeply impressed" with the economic reforms of Argentina, which has beaten back high inflation and stabilized its economy since Carlos Menem became president in 1989. But Gephardt also mentioned the worst side effect of the reforms -- 16.1 percent unemployment.
"While your unemployment is undoubtedly higher than anyone wants, your performance of high growth with no inflation is indeed impressive," Gephardt said.
